item.question: How do Poisson-Binomial distributions relate to modeling infection probabilities?
item.answer: Poisson-Binomial distributions are used to describe the likelihood of different numbers of infections occurring across a population based on varying levels of exposure and susceptibility.

result.gold_answer: Poisson-Binomial distributions are used to describe the likelihood of different numbers of infections occurring across a population based on varying levels of exposure and susceptibility.
result.predicted: The number of infected hosts, I, obeys a Poisson-Binomial distribution, I ∼ Poisson Bin(H, {P_h}) [31]. The mean and variance of the number of infected individuals are then given by E(I) = ∑_{h=1}^H P_h and Var(I) = ∑_{h=1}^H P_h (1 - P_h).
